examples.solution_text:
(a) The denominator requires $x\ne0$. Multiply both sides by $x$.
$\begin{align*}7&=4x\\x&=\frac74\end{align*}$
Check: $7\div\frac74=4$.
(b) First isolate the fraction.
$\begin{align*}\frac{18}{x}&=6\\18&=6x\\x&=3\end{align*}$
The denominator is not zero, and $18/3-2=4$.

(a) $x\ne-3$. Multiply by the whole denominator.
$\begin{align*}14&=4(x+3)\\14&=4x+12\\2&=4x\\x&=\frac12\end{align*}$
Here $x+3=\frac72\ne0$, and $14\div\frac72=4$.
(b) $x\ne5$.
$\begin{align*}15&=-3(5-x)\\15&=-15+3x\\30&=3x\\x&=10\end{align*}$
Check: $15/(5-10)=-3$.

Both denominators require $x\ne0$. Use common denominator $3x$.
$\begin{align*}\frac{15}{3x}+\frac7{3x}&=2\\\frac{22}{3x}&=2\\22&=6x\\x&=\frac{11}{3}\end{align*}$
This is nonzero. Check: $\frac{15}{11}+\frac7{11}=2$.

(a) $x\ne0$.
$\begin{align*}x+15&=-2x\\15&=-3x\\x&=-5\end{align*}$
Check: $(-5+15)/(-5)=-2$.
(b) $x\ne\frac43$.
$\begin{align*}2x+1&=2(3x-4)\\2x+1&=6x-8\\9&=4x\\x&=\frac94\end{align*}$
The denominator is $\frac{11}{4}$, and the numerator is $\frac{11}{2}$. Their quotient is $2$.

The original denominator requires $x\ne-4$. Each side is a single fraction, so cross multiply.
$\begin{align*}7(3x-2)&=5(x+4)\\21x-14&=5x+20\\16x&=34\\x&=\frac{17}{8}\end{align*}$
The numerator is $\frac{35}{8}$ and the denominator is $\frac{49}{8}$, so the original quotient is $\frac57$.

examples.derivation: (a) Multiplying by x gives 7=4x, hence x=7/4≠0; substitution gives 4. (b) Isolating gives 18/x=6, then 18=6x and x=3≠0; substitution gives 18/3−2=4. These adapt the supplied reciprocal examples and isolation exercises.

(a) 14=4(x+3)=4x+12 gives x=1/2; the denominator is 7/2 and the quotient is 4. (b) 15=−3(5−x)=−15+3x gives x=10; the denominator is −5 and the quotient is −3. Both follow the supplied whole-binomial denominator method.
For x≠0, 5/x+7/(3x)=22/(3x). Thus 22=6x and x=11/3. Substitution gives 15/11+7/11=2. This adapts Foundation Q3's common-variable-denominator method.

(a) x+15=−2x gives 15=−3x and x=−5≠0; the quotient is −2. (b) 2x+1=2(3x−4)=6x−8 gives 9=4x and x=9/4. The numerator is 11/2 and denominator 11/4, giving quotient 2 with a nonzero denominator. Both match the supplied linear-numerator exercises.

For x≠−4, clearing both denominators gives 7(3x−2)=5(x+4), then 21x−14=5x+20, 16x=34 and x=17/8. The numerator is 35/8 and denominator 49/8, giving 5/7. This is the supplied denominator-clearing method adapted to the retained assessed fractional-constant form; it introduces no additional skill.
